map.summary: The foundation subsystem is a FastAPI backend for a multi-tenant hybrid RAG service: a create_app entry point exposing health and evaluation routers, a cached typed Settings boundary, an async SQLAlchemy base, a tenant-scoped DocumentService with filesystem storage, and a linear Alembic chain defining identity, content, retrieval, evaluation/audit, and ingestion-job schema. Migrations push authorization, lifecycle, and immutability invariants into PostgreSQL, while containers, Makefile, and CI provide orchestration.
unknowns: No user-facing retrieval or answers HTTP routes are shown in this batch beyond health and the evaluation router mount; the wider application surface is untraced.
Runtime code that populates documents.storage_key/index_version, ingestion_jobs.checkpoint and pipeline_version, and query_traces fields is not present in these sources (F0032, F0064).
Whether the FastAPI health and evaluation endpoints are consumed by a frontend or by external actors is not evidenced.
How Dramatiq workers are started or how Redis is bound to ingestion jobs at runtime is not shown; only the dependency and local Redis container are evidenced (F0042).
The set_updated_at()/prevent_mutation() trigger reuse across later revisions is stated in migration sources, but runtime callers of the affected tables are not present.

diagrams.title: Architecture
diagrams.description: The FastAPI app reads shared Settings and mounts the evaluation router; the backend image runs it via uvicorn, while Makefile and CI drive migrations and tests against the same Base and config.

diagrams.title: Health and readiness
diagrams.description: Liveness shares one handler across two paths; readiness fans out concurrent probes whose boolean results decide 200 versus 503, isolating partial dependency failure.

diagrams.title: Document lifecycle
diagrams.description: DocumentService owns its transactions: upload locks the collection for dedupe and saves files off the event loop; delete commits intent before removing storage, acknowledging non-atomic DB and disk.

diagrams.title: Schema ownership
diagrams.description: Linear Alembic revisions add schema domains; tenant-scoped composite foreign keys enforce ownership, while immutability triggers push retrieval-config, evaluation, judgment, and audit invariants into PostgreSQL.

diagrams.title: Local and CI verification
diagrams.description: Makefile and CI share a local PostgreSQL plus OpenSearch service topology: migrations run first, then seed, then integration and live-provider tests are exercised.

F0001.statement: The backend container builds a Python 3.12 image from backend/pyproject.toml and src, installs the package, and its default CMD runs uvicorn serving hybrid_rag_search.main:app on port 8000 with app-dir /app/src.

F0002.statement: create_app() in hybrid_rag_search.main constructs the FastAPI application, reads settings via get_settings(), and mounts the evaluation router (hybrid_rag_search.evaluation.api.router), making evaluation an HTTP-exposed subsystem.

F0003.statement: module-level `app = create_app()` is the ASGI entry point referenced by both the Docker CMD and the Makefile dev targets.

F0004.statement: Liveness handler `live` is registered on both /health and /health/live, returning HealthResponse with status 'ok' and the configured app_env.

F0005.statement: /health/ready awaits dependency_status(settings); when any dependency boolean is false it sets HTTP 503 and reports status 'not_ready' with a per-dependency dict.

F0006.statement: Alembic env.py derives the database URL from get_settings().database_url through async_database_url(), and sets target_metadata to the SQLAlchemy Base metadata imported from hybrid_rag_search.database, with models imported for side-effect registration.

F0007.statement: Migrations run online asynchronously via async_engine_from_config with NullPool, executing do_run_migrations through connection.run_sync, and offline via literal_binds configuration.

F0008.statement: backend/migrations/README.md documents that Alembic reads DATABASE_URL through application settings, and that db-seed loads deterministic local development records while db-test exercises database constraints against PostgreSQL.

F0009.statement: The Makefile is the central orchestration surface, wiring backend dev (uvicorn main:app), frontend dev, Docker Compose stack lifecycle, Alembic commands, seed/test, tokenizer setup, ingestion recovery, index rebuild start/promote, OpenSearch retrieval integration tests, Cohere live smoke tests, and SciFact/evaluation commands.

F0010.statement: make db-test depends on db-upgrade and runs only pytest -m integration, so integration tests assume a migrated local PostgreSQL.

F0011.statement: CI defines two jobs: a backend job with postgres:17.11 and opensearch:3.6.0 service containers that runs ruff, mypy, pytest, an alembic upgrade/check/downgrade/upgrade cycle, seed (twice), then integration tests; and a frontend job running npm format check, lint, typecheck, test, and build.

F0012.statement: The integration test marker is documented in pyproject.toml as requiring the migrated local PostgreSQL database, and the live marker as making explicitly authorized external provider calls; default pytest runs exclude both and enforce 100% coverage on hybrid_rag_search.

F0013.statement: The project depends on FastAPI/uvicorn for HTTP, SQLAlchemy asyncio with asyncpg and Alembic for persistence, Dramatiq with Redis for background work, Cohere for external provider calls, httpx, pypdf, markdown-it-py, and tokenizers for ingestion and retrieval concerns.

F0014.statement: Local infrastructure is owned by infra/ with root compose.yaml as entry point, pinning ARM64 images for Python, Node, PostgreSQL, Redis, and OpenSearch, with OpenSearch security disabled and published ports bound to 127.0.0.1 for local use only.

F0015.statement: Pre-commit runs repo-local ruff check/fix and ruff format on Python files and Prettier check on frontend files, invoked from the .venv and frontend toolchains.

F0016.statement: A separate CI workflow uses an LLM provider (via KYMA_API_KEY secret and configurable LLM_BASE_URL/LLM_MODEL) plus Graphviz to incrementally regenerate subsystem repository maps and publish them to a dedicated repo-map branch with uploaded artifacts.

F0017.statement: The Alembic migration chain is linear: revision 20260915_01 (identity) has down_revision None, and 20260915_02 (content) and 20260915_03 (retrieval) declare down_revision 20260915_01 and 20260915_02 respectively, so upgrades must apply identity, then content, then retrieval in that order.

F0018.statement: Migration 20260915_01 defines the identity foundation: tenants, users, and memberships tables, with a membership uniquely identifying a (tenant_id, user_id) pair and a role constrained to owner/admin/member.

F0019.statement: Tenant scoping is enforced at the schema level: collections, collection_grants, documents, and query_traces all carry a tenant_id and reference parent tables via composite foreign keys on (tenant_id, id), so a row cannot reference a parent owned by a different tenant.

F0020.statement: Collection-level authorization is modeled by collection_grants, which links a (tenant_id, collection_id) to a membership via composite foreign keys, with permission restricted to read/write/manage and unique per (tenant, collection, membership).

F0021.statement: Documents are owned by a (tenant_id, collection_id) with a composite RESTRICT foreign key to collections, meaning a collection with documents cannot be deleted while those documents exist.

F0022.statement: Document deduplication/identity is anchored by content_hash constrained to a 64-character lowercase hex SHA-256 pattern and indexed via ix_documents_content_hash, and by unique (tenant_id, collection_id, source_key).

F0023.statement: Document lifecycle is encoded by the status column restricted to pending/processing/ready/failed/deleting/deleted, with a check constraint requiring (status = 'deleted') to exactly match (deleted_at IS NOT NULL); index_version is a nonnegative integer tracking reindexing.

F0024.statement: Ingestion jobs are owned by a (tenant_id, document_id) composite CASCADE foreign key to documents, carry queued/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled status, retry counters constrained to 0 <= attempts <= max_attempts with max_attempts > 0, and a JSONB checkpoint for resumable processing.

F0025.statement: retrieval_configs are versioned and immutable: rows are uniquely keyed by (tenant_id, name, version) with version > 0, parameters constrained to a JSONB object, embedding_model nonblank and optional rerank_model, and a trigger trg_retrieval_configs_immutable that calls prevent_mutation() on UPDATE or DELETE to reject any modification.

F0026.statement: query_traces records each retrieval run by referencing both (tenant_id, collection_id) and (tenant_id, retrieval_config_id) with RESTRICT delete semantics, so neither a collection nor a retrieval config can be deleted while traces reference it; a trace stores selected_path, timings, rankings, usage, fallbacks, and an optional error JSONB.

F0027.statement: Query traces enforce a content-capture policy: normalized_query_hash must be a 64-hex SHA-256, and a check constraint requires content_captured to be true or query_text to be NULL, so query text may be omitted while a hash is always retained.

F0028.statement: Migration 20260915_01 creates the set_updated_at() plpgsql trigger function and attaches BEFORE UPDATE triggers to tenants, users, and memberships so updated_at is refreshed server-side on each row update.

F0029.statement: Migration 20260915_02 reuses the set_updated_at() function created by 20260915_01 and attaches the same BEFORE UPDATE trigger to collections, collection_grants, documents, and ingestion_jobs, so these tables depend on the function being defined by the earlier revision.

F0030.statement: Migration 20260915_03 defines an additional prevent_mutation() plpgsql function that raises an integrity_constraint_violation, used only by the retrieval_configs immutability trigger, and its downgrade drops both the trigger and the function.

F0031.statement: Structural invariants are pushed into the database rather than only application code: tenants.slug and collections.slug must match ^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$ and be unique (tenant-scoped for collections), users.email must equal lower(trim(email)) and be unique, and name/display_name fields must be nonblank after trimming.

F0032.statement: Downstream functional subsystems referenced by the foundation (answers, ingestion, retrieval) are expected to operate on this schema, but the migrations themselves only define storage invariants; the runtime code that writes documents.storage_key, index_version, checkpoint, and query_traces fields is not present in these sources.

F0033.statement: Migration 20260915_04 creates four tables: evaluation_datasets, judgments, evaluation_runs, and audit_events, defining the evaluation and audit persistence layer.

F0034.statement: evaluation_datasets is uniquely identified by (tenant_id, name, version) and stores a 64-hex corpus_hash plus JSONB dataset_metadata constrained to be an object.

F0035.statement: judgments reference evaluation_datasets via a composite (tenant_id, dataset_id) foreign key with ON DELETE CASCADE, and carry a per-dataset unique key over query_key, target_type, and target_id.

F0036.statement: evaluation_runs reference evaluation_datasets and retrieval_configs via composite (tenant_id, ...) foreign keys with ON DELETE RESTRICT, and carry a status constrained to queued/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled plus seed, metrics JSONB, error_message, started_at/finished_at.

F0037.statement: audit_events records actor_membership_id (nullable) and enforces a namespaced action regex plus entity_type format, with foreign keys to tenants and memberships using ON DELETE RESTRICT.

F0038.statement: The migration installs a prevent_mutation() trigger on evaluation_datasets, judgments, and audit_events (BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE), making those tables immutable, and a set_updated_at() trigger on evaluation_runs for updated_at maintenance.

F0039.statement: Migration 20260918_05 adds a durable 'stage' column to ingestion_jobs defaulting to 'parse', backfilling succeeded jobs to 'complete', and constraining stage to parse/chunk/embed/index/complete with the invariant (status = 'succeeded') = (stage = 'complete').

F0040.statement: Migration 20260918_06 adds content_hash and pipeline_version to ingestion_jobs, backfills content_hash from documents.content_hash, and enforces a unique (tenant_id, document_id, content_hash, pipeline_version) identity for reusable ingestion recipes.

F0041.statement: Legacy ingestion jobs lacking a pipeline version are assigned a synthesized unique 'pipe_' identity derived from their own job id so they remain recorded but not treated as reusable, per the migration comment.

F0042.statement: Migration 20260918_07 adds expiring worker ownership to ingestion_jobs via lease_token and lease_expires_at, constraining (status = 'running') = (lease_token IS NOT NULL AND lease_expires_at IS NOT NULL) and indexing (status, lease_expires_at).

F0043.statement: Migration 20260918_07 resets pre-migration 'running' ingestion_jobs to 'queued' so rows without a verifiable live owner are recoverable rather than leased to an unknown worker.

F0044.statement: Migration 20260918_08 adds next_attempt_at to ingestion_jobs with a check that it may only be set while status = 'queued', and indexes (status, next_attempt_at) for retry eligibility scanning.

F0045.statement: The Alembic chain is linear: 20260915_04 revises 20260915_03, and the ingestion-job migrations form 20260918_05 → 06 → 07 → 08 each revising its predecessor.

F0046.statement: Settings (pydantic BaseSettings) defines a single runtime configuration boundary covering database_url, redis_url, and opensearch URLs/aliases, BM25/dense candidate limits, rerank limits, retrieval_deadline_seconds, filesystem roots (storage_root, tokenizer_root, ingestion_artifact_root), and Cohere model/timeout/cost parameters.

F0047.statement: Settings.validate_cross_field_settings enforces startup-time invariants pairing model and index dimensions and bounding reranking: embed-english-light-v3.0 requires 384 dimensions, rerank_result_limit may not exceed rerank_candidate_limit, and the Cohere rerank timeout may not exceed retrieval_deadline_seconds.

F0048.statement: get_settings() is lru_cache-wrapped, so Settings is constructed once per process as the shared configuration source.

F0049.statement: database.py provides a shared SQLAlchemy DeclarativeBase subclass `Base` whose MetaData applies a project-wide constraint/index naming convention (ix, uq, ck, fk, pk), and this Base is documented as used by both application models and Alembic migrations.

F0050.statement: async_database_url rewrites a plain 'postgresql' URL to 'postgresql+asyncpg' and passes through any other driver name unchanged, so callers can supply a synchronous-style URL and get the async driver.

F0051.statement: models/__init__.py re-exports model classes across four modules (content, evaluation, identity, retrieval) as a single import surface, indicating a shared domain model package arranged by subdomain (collections/documents/ingestion, evaluation/audit, tenancy/identity, retrieval config/trace).

F0052.statement: DocumentService owns its transactions via an async_sessionmaker and a FileStorage dependency injected in the constructor; callers must pass an already authorized tenant/collection scope, so authorization is a caller responsibility rather than service-internal.

F0053.statement: DocumentService.upload computes a SHA-256 content_hash, takes a SELECT ... with_for_update lock on the Collection row to serialize duplicate checks across concurrent uploads, and returns duplicate=True with the existing document ID when a non-deleting document with the same hash exists in that collection.

F0054.statement: DocumentService.upload writes the file via asyncio.to_thread(self.storage.save, ...) inside the session context (after flush), so filesystem I/O runs off the event loop; the class docstring states PostgreSQL and disk cannot commit atomically and a crash may leave an orphan file but must never delete a possibly committed original.

F0055.statement: DocumentService.delete uses two separate transactions: first committing status DELETING, then deleting the storage object and marking DELETED with deleted_at set, a sequence the code comments describe as committing intent first so an I/O failure leaves a durable retryable state.

F0056.statement: DocumentService mutating/fetching methods re-validate stored storage_key against storage_key(tenant_id, document_id) and reject mismatches, defending against a corrupted or cross-tenant storage pointer.

F0057.statement: DocumentService.fetch and _document raise domain-specific errors: DocumentNotFound (LookupError) when no document/collection exists in tenant scope, and DocumentUnavailable (ValueError) when the document is DELETING or DELETED.

F0058.statement: health.py defines three independent dependency probes—check_postgres (asyncpg connect + SELECT 1), check_redis (Redis PING), check_opensearch (HTTP GET /_cluster/health with raise_for_status)—and dependency_status runs them concurrently via asyncio.gather, mapping results to keys 'postgres','redis','opensearch'.

F0059.statement: run_check wraps each probe in a broad try/except Exception returning False, so any probe failure degrades that single dependency to an unready result rather than propagating.

F0060.statement: The content schema uses composite tenant-scoped foreign keys (ForeignKeyConstraint on tenant_id plus a child key into multi-column unique constraints) across collections, documents, and ingestion_jobs, so cross-tenant references are structurally prevented at the database level.

F0061.statement: CollectionGrant links a membership to a collection with permission constrained to read/write/manage, defined as a DB check constraint, with a unique constraint on (tenant_id, collection_id, membership_id) and a tenant/membership index.

F0062.statement: The Document model enforces SHA-256 hex format on content_hash, nonblank source_key/storage_key, allowed status values, and a bidirectional constraint tying status='deleted' to deleted_at IS NOT NULL, with indexes on content_hash and (tenant_id, status).

F0063.statement: IngestionJob models an asynchronous ingestion workflow with status/stage enums, attempts vs max_attempts, JSONB checkpoint state, and lease_token/lease_expires_at; constraints enforce that status 'running' implies a lease, 'succeeded' implies stage 'complete', next_attempt_at is only set when queued, and attempts stay within max_attempts.

F0064.statement: IngestionJob uniqueness is keyed on (tenant_id, document_id, content_hash, pipeline_version) with pipeline_version constrained to the format 'pipe_<64 hex>', indicating ingestion identity is derived from content and a versioned pipeline recipe; how that pipeline_version value is computed at runtime is not shown in these sources.
